extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and research communities using OSF registrations / open science practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and criteria for earning Open Science badges on OSF registrations by linking research resources (data, materials, code, papers, supplements). Includes what qualifies for each badge and the workflow to add linked resources via DOI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Data badge
rubrics_metrics.description: The Open Data badge is awarded when digitally-shareable data necessary to reproduce the reported results are publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data must be publicly available and digitally-shareable such that others can reproduce reported results. Earn the badge by linking the data to your registration via a DOI (see workflow guidance). The badge will be displayed on your registration and in search results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Materials badge
rubrics_metrics.description: The Open Materials badge is earned by making publicly available the components of the research methodology needed to reproduce the reported procedure and analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials should include methodological components necessary to reproduce procedure and analysis. Make them publicly available and link them to your registration with a DOI to receive the badge; the badge will be shown on the registration and in search results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Analytic Code badge
rubrics_metrics.description: The Open Analytic Code badge is earned by making publicly available the analytical code needed to reproduce the reported analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analytic code required to reproduce analyses must be publicly accessible and linked via DOI to the registration. Once linked, the appropriate badge/icon is displayed on the registration and in search results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Papers badge
rubrics_metrics.description: The Papers badge is earned when any manuscripts, preprints, post-prints, reports, or peer reviewed publications that were generated from the study are made publicly available and linked using a DOI to your registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Qualifying items include manuscripts, preprints, post-prints, reports, or peer-reviewed publications generated from the study. These must be publicly available and linked to the registration with a DOI to earn the badge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplements badge
rubrics_metrics.description: The Supplements badge is earned when any other resources that are created from a study that do not align with any of the previous items are made publicly available and linked using a DOI to your registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Supplements badge for resources that don't fit Data/Materials/Code/Papers. Make them publicly available and link via DOI to the registration to receive the badge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Badge-earning procedure (link resources via DOI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Earning these badges are as easy as linking open research resources to your registration via a DOI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Workflow: go to your registration -> click “Resources” -> click to add your new resource -> enter the DOI for the resource. The appropriate badge/icon is then displayed on your registration and in search results. Resources can be on or off OSF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking works on- and off-OSF
rubrics_metrics.description: Link resources, both on and off OSF, to your registrations and make it even easier to share your research plan and materials!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOIs from external repositories are accepted; linking external resources to registrations still earns the badges and makes resources discoverable via the registration and search results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Badges as incentive and norming mechanism (Theory of Change)
rubrics_metrics.description: Using badges to signal open practice adoption is both an incentive to reward adoption of transparent behaviors, and also a norming activity that can shift communities towards adoption of open behaviors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Badges are framed as part of a coordinated approach (Policy, Incentives, Communities, User experience, Infrastructure) to change research culture. Displaying badges on registrations and search results is intended to reward and normalize open practices across communities.
